finding: The server ships a theme router with applyPreset/list/save/delete and the editor calls NONE of them — the only editor→dashboard calls are cms, media stock, siteComponents, siteDetail.domains, siteVersions, userTemplates and webhooks. Brand starters and presets are client-only.
evidence: server/trpc/routers/theme.ts (12 procedures, key `theme` per server/trpc/router.ts); zero matches for client().theme.* across packages/editor/src; sibling sync services exist for cms (services/cmsSync.ts), components (componentSync.ts) and templates (templateSync.ts) — there is no themeSync.ts
fix: Decide whether brand presets are meant to be shared across a workspace. If yes, the design needs a board for a SERVER-side preset list (someone else's preset, an org preset) which no board currently draws; if no, the four theme procedures are dead server code and should be recorded as such.

finding: Per-page translations have a complete server API — pages.setTranslation / getTranslation / removeTranslation — with no caller anywhere in the repo, while a Settings · Localization board exists. The screen is designed and the API is built; nothing joins them.
evidence: server/trpc/routers/pages.ts declares setTranslation, getTranslation, removeTranslation; a scan of all 225 distinct tRPC paths actually invoked across packages/, app/, lib/, components/ and server/ contains none of them
fix: Either the Localization board must draw the per-page translation surface those procedures serve (which page, which locale, what happens to an untranslated page), or the procedures are dead. Check with the founder which.

finding: sites.saveProjectData and sites.getProjectData have no caller in the repo — they exist only in their own router and its unit test. The shipping save path is saveProjectFromEditor. Dead server code, not a missing door: do not design screens for them.
evidence: grep for saveProjectData|getProjectData across the repo returns only server/trpc/routers/sites.ts:516,541 and server/trpc/routers/__tests__/site-limit-message.test.ts:41-42, which mocks saveProjectFromEditor alongside
fix: Record as dead server code. No design work.

finding: media.moveFolder has no caller — moving a folder (as opposed to moving assets INTO a folder) has a server procedure and no UI or board.
evidence: server/trpc/routers/media.ts declares moveFolder; not present among the 225 invoked tRPC paths. Note the editor DOES call media.searchStockPhotos/searchStockVideos, so the media client wiring exists and this is a specific gap, not an unwired module.
fix: Confirm with the Media agent's board walk whether any board draws folder reorganisation. If not, this is a designed-in-the-API, undesigned-in-the-file capability.

finding: ai.getQuotaStatus has no caller, yet the AI section has an error-quota board. The board depicts a quota state the editor never asks the server about.
evidence: server/trpc/routers/ai.ts declares getQuotaStatus; absent from the 225 invoked paths. The editor's only AI network calls are the literal paths /api/trpc/ai.summarize and /api/trpc/ai.milestoneSuggest (packages/editor/src/editor/panels/version-history/useAISummary.ts:10, :180 region)
fix: Either wire the quota board to the procedure that serves it, or establish how the quota state is actually reached and correct the board's premise.

finding: siteComponents.usage has no caller while its four siblings (list/get/upsert/delete) are all called by componentSync. 'Which pages use this component?' is the question a user must answer before editing or deleting a master, the server can answer it, and nothing asks.
evidence: the 225 invoked paths include siteComponents.list/get/upsert/delete and NOT siteComponents.usage; server/trpc/routers/site-component.ts declares it
fix: A usage/impact board before destructive component edits. Build it from the detach-confirm modal 1170:4792, which is the nearest existing 'this affects other things' surface.

finding: templates.cloneFromSite has no caller — 'start a new site from an existing one' is built on the server and has neither UI nor board. templates.generate.{create,cancel,status} ARE called, so the AI-generation half of this router is wired and the clone half is not.
evidence: invoked paths include templates.generate.create / .cancel / .status; templates.cloneFromSite absent
fix: Confirm whether cloning is in scope for the editor at all — it may belong to the dashboard. If dashboard-only, it is out of this file's scope and should be recorded as such rather than boarded.

finding: Client sign-off is the only TERMINAL module in the file: 3 inbound cross-module edges and ZERO outbound. The client approves and the flow stops there — nothing returns to the agency, to Review, to Publish, or to the editor.
evidence: module-graph over all 3,077 prototype edges resolved to (source section -> destination section): 19 · Client sign-off in=3 out=0. Every other non-archive section has outbound edges. Corroborates W-E-01 at the graph level, which found ReviewTab has no APPROVED branch at all (ReviewTab.tsx:683 branches only for changes_requested) — so both the drawing and the code stop at the same place.
fix: The approved round must lead somewhere. The two candidates the file already contains: back to the agency's Review panel in an approved state (which W-E-16 says has no board), or forward to Publish, which is what approval is FOR. Whichever, the section needs at least one outbound edge.

finding: The Inspector has 26 boards and only 9 inbound cross-module edges — the lowest in-degree of any built module except Components (5), Command palette (3) and Ecommerce (2). The panel where every element is actually edited is the hardest one to reach in the prototype.
evidence: module-graph in-degree over all 3,077 edges: Inspector in=9 out=21. Compare Brand in=123, Content in=108, Media in=107, Layers in=110 — all panels of similar size. Independently corroborated by W-I-01, which found the three pill dropdowns are the only door to four finished Inspector boards and have no open-state board.
fix: Selecting an element on any canvas board should reach the Inspector. Today that edge exists on a handful of boards; the rail-and-drawer chrome carries the other panels everywhere and the Inspector is the one it does not.

finding: The Journeys section is the file's busiest hub — in=249, out=313, reaching 21 of 29 sections — which means the S-flow narrative is doing the work of connecting modules that do not connect to each other directly. That is fine as a narrative device and a problem if it is mistaken for product wiring.
evidence: module-graph: Journeys in=249 out=313; by contrast Content out=4, Brand out=3, AI out=3, Review out=2, Layers out=4. The panels are near-terminal; the journeys carry the flow.
fix: No change. Recorded so that a future reader does not conclude the modules are well connected because the edge count is high — 1,560 of 3,077 edges are cross-module and a large share of those pass through Journeys or through rail chrome, not through a product step.

finding: Five printed chords name commands with no binding anywhere: ⌃G (Group, 1176:4898), ⌘⇧↑ (Insert Before, :4906), ⌘⇧↓ (Insert After, :4910), ⌘⇧W (Wrap in Section, :4920), ⌘⇧U (Unwrap, :4924). insertActions.ts has no `shortcut:` field at all and no group binding exists in useCanvasKeyboard.ts.
evidence: grep for a shortcut field in src/editor/canvas/menus/actions/insertActions.ts returns nothing; no 'g' chord in src/editor/canvas/hooks/useCanvasKeyboard.ts. Distinct from the three chords fixed today (1175:4862, 1175:4863, 1176:4894), which named a chord the app honours for a DIFFERENT command — Alt+Arrow reorders (useCanvasKeyboard.ts:261,274) while bare Arrow navigates (:287-289, :298-300).
fix: Two honest options and they are a product decision, not a correction: remove the glyphs so the menu stops promising a shortcut, or build the bindings. ⌘⇧↑ in particular currently nudges the element 1px, so printing it against Insert Before is the same class of defect just fixed — recommend deciding this one rather than leaving it.

finding: 112 hotspot rows across 49 boards sit outside a board whose clipsContent is true. If the file is walked in PRESENTATION mode those hotspots are not rendered and not clickable, so every state they are the only door to is unreachable — which is how Modal · Add Child Element (1706:8501) ended up with its sole inbound edge on an invisible node.
evidence: Measured with scripts/figma/find-unreachable-hotspots.mjs: for every FRAME with clipsContent=true, any direct child named hotspot/* whose absolute bounds fall below or right of the board. 112 across 49 boards, e.g. 1344:7165 'S7.2 · Branding · pointer' (720x560) with hotspot/back overhanging 294px, and five Webhooks state rows overhanging 36px each. Confirms the Inspector instance of this class independently (W-I-05, five hotspots at y=820 on an 812-tall board) — the Brand fix applied earlier today did NOT reach these.
fix: DO NOT bulk-move them yet, and this is the reason: the hotspot frames have no fill, but many carry a visible TEXT child naming the state ('collection-created · toast'). Re-seating those inside would print 112 labels onto 49 boards. The label-less ones (e.g. 444:2388, already inside 170:2, which renders clean) can be moved safely; the labelled ones need the label hidden or the destination given a second door. Settle first whether the file is reviewed in presentation mode or on canvas — on canvas these are all reachable and none of this is a defect.
